tasks.objective: Fix the consumer side of the timeout seam: implement job_timeout in pipeline/consumer.py to resolve the frozen wire key timeout_ms first, then the deprecated draft 'timeout' key as fallback, then DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (30000); add unit tests in tests/test_consumer.py covering the resolution order (timeout_ms primary, legacy fallback, both-keys priority, default) while leaving every existing test case in the repo unmodified and green.

concepts: job wire dict shape {id, payload, timeout_ms} passed by reference (no serializer)
the draft 'timeout' key is consumer-side only and has no in-repo emitter (frozen assumption A-3)
engine uses the strict comparison work_ms > timeout_ms with status literals 'done'/'timeout' (frozen, must stay untouched)
unittest-style tests executed with pytest from the repo root; new tests are additive only

forbidden_scope: pipeline/producer.py: read-only reference for the wire contract - no rename, no signature change, no default change
pipeline/engine.py: read-only - no semantic or cosmetic change (task constraint)
tests/test_producer.py and tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py: read-only for T01 - no modification of existing test cases
removing or re-keying DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS (it stays defined with value 30000 in consumer.py)
no new files, no new modules, no new dependencies
inputs: frozen contract C1 (job wire schema) from stage-contract.json
frozen contract C2 (consumer timeout resolution order, owned by T01) from stage-contract.json
baseline defect evidence: pytest tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py::TestPipelineE2E::test_pipeline_e2e_effective_timeout fails with 30000 != 500
outputs: pipeline/consumer.py: job_timeout resolving timeout_ms -> 'timeout' -> DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS; validate_job and DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS behavior unchanged
tests/test_consumer.py: existing cases untouched plus new test methods covering timeout_ms primary, legacy fallback, both-keys priority, and default resolution
tasks.split_rationale: the consumer module plus its own unit tests is the minimal context closure for the defect: the fix, the contract it implements (C2), and its unit-level proof all live in the same two files plus the wire contract (C1); the cross-module e2e proof is cut at the stable unit/e2e test boundary into T02, which must run after this fix lands because it asserts the fixed behavior.

tasks.objective: Close the producer -> consumer e2e seam with regression tests: extend tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py with cases asserting the frozen resolution order at the seam (producer's timeout_ms reaches the consumer; both keys present -> timeout_ms wins; legacy timeout-only job falls back; no timeout key -> default 30000) and verify the entire suite (producer, consumer, engine, e2e) passes with engine semantics unchanged and no existing test case modified.

concepts: producer -> consumer pass-through of the same job dict (no serializer; jobs must be built via producer.make_job for wire-path fidelity)
the two pre-existing e2e test methods must stay byte-identical; new cases are additive inside the existing test file
engine status literals 'done'/'timeout' with the strict > comparison are frozen (C1) and must not be re-asserted beyond the existing engine e2e case
tests/test_consumer.py shows which resolution behaviors are already covered at unit level, so e2e cases must not duplicate them

forbidden_scope: pipeline/: all modules are read-only for T02 - if the suite is red after T01, that is a T01 defect or a CONTRACT_CHANGE_REQUEST against C2, not a T02 code fix
the two pre-existing e2e test methods: no modification, no rename, no skip
tests/test_producer.py and tests/test_consumer.py: owned by other tasks, no edits
no new test files, no new dependencies
inputs: T01 output: pipeline/consumer.py with job_timeout resolving timeout_ms first (consumed, never patched, by the new e2e cases)
frozen contracts C1 (job wire schema) and C2 (resolution order) from stage-contract.json
outputs: tests/test_pipeline_e2e.py: existing cases untouched plus new seam regression test methods (timeout_ms reaches consumer via producer.make_job; both-keys priority; legacy-only fallback; no-key default)
full-suite-green evidence: pytest tests/ exits 0 with 0 failed
tasks.split_rationale: the e2e suite is the stable test boundary between unit-level proof (T01) and cross-module seam proof: it is the only closure where producer output meets consumer parsing, the ablation removes the integration task that would normally own this path, and the seam regression cases are meaningless until T01's fixed consumer lands (hence the verification edge T01 -> T02); the cut is at the unit/e2e test boundary, not inside a module.
